Cause: The pod's image name is misspelled. The deployment references `registry.internal/serach-indexer:1.3.2` (note "serach" instead of "search"), so the registry returns "manifest unknown" and the kubelet reports ImagePullBackOff. ImagePullBackOff means the container could not start because Kubernetes could not pull the image, typically due to an invalid image name or missing pull credentials [cite: concepts/containers/images#imagepullbackoff-0]. Since no container ever started, there are no application logs.

Evidence: In namespace `search`, pod `search-indexer-7b5d8-zt6qn` is in ImagePullBackOff with message: `Back-off pulling image "registry.internal/serach-indexer:1.3.2": manifest unknown`.

Fix: Correct the image name in the Deployment's pod template from `serach-indexer` to `search-indexer` (e.g. `kubectl -n search set image deploy/search-indexer <container>=registry.internal/search-indexer:1.3.2`) and re-apply. The new pod should pull successfully and become ready.
